content:
incident-bot: PAGER: KV cache hit-rate collapsed on pool-gamma, continuous-batching latency spike > SLO. 95th token latency 1.8s (SLO 1.2s). Autoscaler oscillation signal active.

janet: ack — I'm looking. seeing sustained batch sizes jump from ~4 to 40 for some prefixes.

suhail: oncall here, collecting logs + metrics. pulling kvcache metrics and recent deploys. any customer reports?

maria: noticed an uptick in hosted-api 5xx-ish throttles from a few keys. reported by internal client test. no major error burst, mostly timeouts.

janet: quick hypothesis: prefix-growth leak — lots of new prefixes hitting hot-KV and continuous batching keeps prefetching + keeping big KV entries alive which increases RT. that raises CPU/GPU and HPA flips.

karen: @janet can you confirm whether this lines up with the 02:10 rolling canary? deploy-bot says model-runtime config changed at 02:07 (batch.max=64 -> 128, continuous_batching=on).

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: runtime-config updated by ops-release at 2075300900. Changed batch.max to 128, continuous_batching toggled ON for pool-gamma.

janet: yep that matches. I'm rolling a small config hotfix to reduce batch.max and disable the aggressive prefill. will dry-run on canary nodes.

suhail: logs (snip):
```
E 02:23:45 kvcache.cpp:231 prefix_inserted prefix=usr:freeplan:abcd size=2.4MB
W 02:24:01 batch_scheduler.cpp:89 batch_size=36 latency=1.22s
I 02:24:05 autoscaler: scale_event up->down thrash_count=4
```

janet: starting hotfix: set `runtime.batch.max=8` and `runtime.continuous_prefill=false` on canary (pool-gamma-canary). applying now.

maria: flagging customer-impact: small number of enterprise customers seeing token latency spikes in the last 20m (approx 0.7% of requests). CS notified for slow API responses; no data exfiltration.

lee: I'm available for handoff in 30m — if this lasts will take next shift.

janet: canary patch applied. monitoring.

(2m pass)

janet: canary metrics look better: mean batch size down from 38->7, 95th latency dropped to 1.1s. good signal.

suhail: rolling hotfix to pool-gamma primary now. will push change to remaining nodes with rolling update and fog-backoff.

karen: note to ops: HPA minReplicas currently 3, observed thrash when replicas hit 6 and drop quickly. suggest temporary hysteresis increase.

janet: temporary mitigation: bump HPA minReplicas to 6 and increase scale-down stabilization to 5m to avoid flip-flopping. executing now.

deploy-bot: Config change: HPA minReplicas set to 6, scaleDownStabilizationSeconds=300 by janet at 2075301410.

maria: confirm: customer-facing latency improved after hotfix? CS reports degraded requests decreased to baseline.

janet: yes, from 0.7% impacted -> ~0.05% during roll. still watching.

suhail: a couple of follow-ups I already spotted:
- prefix TTLs are too long for ephemeral workloads (some prefixes keep sticking in the cache)
- continuous prefill policy lacks guards for prefix cardinality
- batch.max change didn't have preflight load tests for streaming/kv pattern

karen: good notes. we should open a follow-up ticket for longer-term fixes.

lee: taking over monitoring and watch for 1hr. handoff: janet -> lee. please @me if anything regresses.

janet: handing off. summary for post-incident notes:
- root cause: aggressive runtime change (batch.max=128 + continuous_prefill on) combined with high new-prefix traffic -> KV cache amplification -> increased per-request latency -> HPA oscillation.
- mitigation: rollback/patch to batch.max=8, disabled continuous_prefill, bumped HPA min replicas and scale-down stabilization, prefill disabled for unknown high-card prefixes.
- customer impact: transient latency spike affecting ~0.7% of hosted API requests for ~25m; no errors or data loss; CS notified.

maria: filing customer notification draft, pinging CS.

suhail: opening follow-ups: DEVOPS-4521 (add preflight tests for batch config), RUNTIME-387 (prefix TTLs + cardinality guard), HPA-ops-99 (adaptive hysteresis based on batching signal).

karen: linking runbook updates: add a step to verify prefix-cardinality and run `kvcache-stats --hot-prefixes` before enabling high batch.max on any pool.

lee: watching for 10m, then will close thread unless anything else.

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2 at 2075301660; auto-pager quiet for 10m.

lee: closing note: please add regression test for continuous_prefill with synthetic prefix storms. assign owners in the follow-ups.

janet: thanks team. I'll draft the postmortem and include graphs + timeline.

maria: will coordinate CS comms once postmortem is ready.

(END)
